briefdescription.para: The stable time increment of the central difference method for a continuum element, from the largest eigenfrequency of the element.

detaileddescription.para: The central difference method with a lumped mass $\mathbf{M}$ is stable for $\Delta t \leq 2 / \omega_{\max}$, with the largest eigenfrequency $\omega_{\max}$ of the assembled system, and the largest eigenfrequency of the system is bounded by the largest of its elements: $\omega_{\max}^2 \leq \max_e \lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{M}_e^{-1} \mathbf{K}_e)$. An element's own eigenvalue is therefore a safe estimate, for every polynomial order, every quadrature rule and every distortion, since it is computed from the element's own strain operator and its own lumped mass where a characteristic length over a wave speed is the exact limit of a linear bar only.

The stiffness of an isotropic elastic element splits along the two Lame constants, \[ \mathbf{K}_e = \lambda\, \mathbf{K}_\lambda + \mu\, \mathbf{K}_\mu, \qquad \mathbf{K}_\lambda = \int \mathbf{b}\, \mathbf{b}^T \,\mathrm{d}V, \qquad \mathbf{K}_\mu = \int \mathbf{B}^T \mathbf{D}\, \mathbf{B} \,\mathrm{d}V, \] with the strain operator $\mathbf{B}$ in Voigt notation, the divergence $\mathbf{b}^T$ (the sum of its rows of the normal strains) and $\mathbf{D}$ = 2 on the normal and 1 on the engineering shear strains, so that $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{K}_e \mathbf{u} = \int \lambda (
abla \cdot \mathbf{u})^2 + 2 \mu\,  oldsymbol{\varepsilon} :  oldsymbol{\varepsilon} \,\mathrm{d}V$. ( $\mathbf{K}_\mu$ is not the deviatoric operator: $2\, oldsymbol{\varepsilon} :  oldsymbol{\varepsilon}$ contains the volumetric strain too.) A material tells its largest wave speed $c$, i.e. the P-wave modulus $ho c^2 = \lambda + 2\mu$, but not how it divides into $\lambda$ and $\mu$. With $\lambda = ho c^2 - 2\mu$, the stiffness is affine in $\mu \in [0, ho c^2 / 2]$ ( $
u \in [0, 1/2]$), and the largest eigenvalue of a matrix is convex in it, so it is largest at one of the two ends: the incompressible end $ho c^2\, \mathbf{K}_\lambda$ or the end without lateral contraction $ho c^2 \mathbf{K}_\mu / 2$. Hence \[ \omega_{\max}^2 \leq ho c^2\, \Lambda, \qquad \Lambda = \max\Big( \lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{M}_e^{-1} \mathbf{K}_\lambda),\; 	frac{1}{2} \lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{M}_e^{-1} \mathbf{K}_\mu) \Big), \qquad \Delta t =  rac{2}{\sqrt{ho c^2\, \Lambda}} . \] The bound is exact for a material at the end whose term is the larger one and conservative everywhere else, by as much as a compact linear element at $
u = 0$, where the incompressible end governs (its time increment is then about 0.6 of the element's true one). It assumes an isotropic material with the same $
u$ at all quadrature points of the element, $
u \geq 0$, and takes the largest P-wave modulus of its quadrature points.
A plane stress section is covered by the plane operators: its in-plane modulus $2\lambda\mu / (\lambda + 2\mu)$ is smaller than $\lambda$.
